reason: I already cook for my family every Sunday and know dishes like tom yum and pad see ew, and when I want something new, YouTube is free. I might try the free green curry, but paying 99 baht for recipes doesn't fit how I save money.
objection: Will it really come out better than a free YouTube video? The free dishes are ones I already cook, so they don't prove the paid ones will come out right, and if one of my Sunday dishes fails I've wasted ingredients meant for several days.
would_change_my_mind: Let me try one Sunday cook-ahead plan for free: if the three dishes really keep all week, my family eats them, and the shopping list costs less than what I spend now at my market, I'd pay the 99 baht.
